email.subject: New sign-in to your TeamChat account

body.v: We detected a sign-in to your TeamChat account from a new device. If it was you, there's nothing you need to do.
If it wasn't you, open the TeamChat app yourself, go to Settings, then Devices, and sign that device out.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in teamchat.example, the real domain.
"If it was you, there's nothing you need to do." No threat, no deadline.
Instead of a link, it gives you the route through the app, to follow yourself.
No link, no button: nothing in this message can capture your login details.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: TeamChat: the address is on its real domain, teamchat.example.
choices: A colleague putting you to the test

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Hardly any. The tone is calm, and if the sign-in was yours, that's the end of it.

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing for now. If the sign-in wasn't yours, it tells you to go into the app yourself.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Pay for an option to secure the account
Nothing, except checking the app if needed

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: The message gives you the steps itself: open the TeamChat app and look at your devices.
choices: Reply to say it wasn't you
Forward it to a friend first
Open the app yourself and check your devices

actions.label: Open the TeamChat app yourself and look at your devices
actions.consequence: You see your phone and your computer. Nothing to report.

actions.label: Ignore it: you recognise the new device
actions.consequence: The sign-in was yours. There was nothing to do.

actions.label: Reply to the email to say it wasn't you
actions.consequence: Nobody reads replies sent to this address. If the sign-in wasn't yours, the app is where you act.

attacker_reveal: Genuine, I'll grant you. TeamChat's domain, not a single link, and it sends you into the app under your own steam. A security alert can be real: this one asks for nothing, and that's how you tell.
